titulo.texto: The East Gallery and the Tower

frase_gancho.texto: A date carved into the columns, a view of the volcanoes, and a tower that returned to its place five years after the earthquake.

puente_narrativo.texto: Follow your route: it may take you to Hidalgo Street or all the way to the Casa de Cantinflas.

guion_corto.texto: Fifteen thirty-five. That year is carved into the columns of the east gallery, as a completion date for the work on the palace. Here, beneath the arches, the building offers its best view: the terrace opens toward the city and toward the volcanoes. It is the same corridor where Rivera’s mural is found, and the restored triptych occupies its original place. From here you can also see the tower, the cylindrical tower at the Northwest corner, about fifteen meters tall. The earthquake of two thousand seventeen damaged it, and in two thousand twenty-two it returned to its place with lighter materials, with seventy percent less weight. It is the closing piece of the upper part of the palace.

guion_largo.texto:
Numbers keep secrets. On the columns of the east gallery on the second floor there is a carved date: fifteen thirty-five. According to the INAH record, it marks the year the construction of the palace was completed. If you look closely, it is an old way of signing a building.

The gallery is what remains of the oldest core of the palace. According to a description from the museum, the first core, from the time of the encomienda, consisted of three large halls and a terrace with arches that looked toward the volcanoes. Today you are still walking along that terrace. It is the same place where Diego Rivera painted in nineteen thirty, and where the restored triptych is displayed once again since the reopening of two thousand twenty-three.

It is worth pausing here and looking outside. The arcaded corridors are not just decoration. They let the air through, give shade, and offer a view. Cortés chose Cuernavaca for its climate and its fertile lands, and from this terrace the choice makes sense.

You can also see the tower. It is a cylindrical tower at the Northwest corner of the palace, about fifteen meters tall, which was added in the late nineteenth century. It is what gives the building its castle-like silhouette, and it is the most photographed element. The earthquake of September nineteenth, two thousand seventeen, damaged it. Five years later, in two thousand twenty-two, it was raised again. To make it safer, it was rebuilt with lighter materials and ended up with seventy percent less weight. With that work, the architectural part of the restoration was concluded.

The director of the INBAL, Lucina Jiménez, said at the reopening that the building is one of the most important colonial constructions in the country. She described it as a fortress that once yielded to nature. That idea sums up well what you have seen today: a palace that has fallen and been raised again many times.

The Rivera mural in this gallery also went through difficult years. It was protected between nineteen ninety-three and nineteen ninety-five, and the restored triptych is on display again in its original place since the reopening.

At that ceremony, the director of the INAH, Diego Prieto, said that the museum must represent all the peoples of Morelos. He also said that these peoples must be heard in their own languages, songs, and dances. He described it as a plural space that speaks of the community’s present. The gallery, with its view and its history, is a good place to think about that idea.

Before leaving the gallery, look up and to the sides. The stone, the arches, and the date of fifteen thirty-five have been there for almost five centuries. Rivera, Cortés, Morelos, and Zapata looked, each in their own way, upon this same view.

texto: Find the date carved into the columns of the east gallery
Look from the terrace toward the city and the volcanoes and think about why Cortés chose this place
Locate the cylindrical tower at the Northwest corner and notice that it looks like stone, even though it is lighter

texto.Carved date: 1535, marks the year the construction was completed
texto.Tower: cylindrical, about 15 m, Northwest corner, added in the late 19th century

texto.pregunta: Myth: The tower is part of Cortés’s original construction.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It was added in the late nineteenth century. After the 2017 earthquake, it was raised again with lighter materials.
